docs.title: 2.6 Machine Learning (ML) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0

The metadata for Machine Learning (ML) data (MatCore-ML) is tabulated below. This metadata documents key aspects of the ML method to provide understanding of the dataset generated by it. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the ML computations it describes. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — ml-task*

Characterization of the machine learning process performed.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The nature of the machine learning task.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Property prediction, Structure generation, Synthesis prediction, Ranking, Clustering, Embedding. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Property prediction" – Values of a property predicted for given materials or structures, e.g. formation energies or band gaps
  • "Structure generation" – New structures produced by the model, freely or for a given composition, space group or target property, including crystal structure prediction for a given composition
  • "Synthesis prediction" – Routes, precursors or conditions predicted for making a given material
  • "Ranking" – Given materials or structures ordered by a predicted score, e.g. to select candidates for further calculation
  • "Clustering" – Given materials or structures grouped by similarity
  • "Embedding" – A numerical representation computed for each given material or structure, for use by other models or analyses

Note: This Property can be repeated if the machine learning task involves multiple types of calculations.

Note: A machine-learned interatomic potential is not described here; it is a particle interaction model (pim, theory-level Machine-learned).

Note: Structures generated by a model learned from data are described here, guided or not. Structures built by rules the author specifies, with no such model, are a computation of method GC.

description

Explanation of the machine learning task performed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — ml-model*

A comprehensive description of the machine learning approach and architecture used.

Required Repeatable yes no

Note: An inference computation whose model is trained in another computation of the record gives only algorithm and target-variable, to identify the model; the training computation's settings describe the rest.

algorithm*

The machine learning method used.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Neural network, Random forest, Gaussian process.

target-variable*

The desired output or answer the machine learning model aims to predict.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — input-feature

Information provided to the machine learning method.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: The form and meaning of an input variable or feature, e.g. a graph representation of a crystal structure, including any feature engineering performed to define it (e.g. dimensionality reduction, clustering).

model-architecture

A description of the network topology used by the specified algorithm.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. for a neural network, the kinds of layers and how they are connected. Explain the role of each architecture-parameter entry.

architecture-parameter

A fixed variable that defines the architecture of the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the number of layers, the number of nodes per layer, a cutoff radius or a maximum body order. Training settings are hyperparameter entries of training-method.

name*

The designation of the architecture parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the architecture parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the architecture parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — model-size

The number of trainable parameters of the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

training-data

The information used for parameterizing the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

Name of the training dataset used to train in the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — contents*

Description of the information included in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. DFT calculations or experiments, and what one item of the data is (a structure, a configuration), since size counts items.

source

Location from which the training data was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A MatCore ID, web address, DOI, citation, or other description of where the data was obtained. Training data produced by a computation of the record is not given here: the training computation names it in minimal computation › input with the role Training data.

size

Number of items in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

Clarifications: The kind of item is stated in contents.

data-preprocessing

Approach used for preliminary refining of raw, unformatted, or incomplete information into a structured and clean state suitable for modeling or analysis.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — missing-data

Documentation of incomplete, null, or unrecorded entries within a feature set that hinder algorithm training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the percentage of missing data, and which fields are missing and why.

missing-data-strategy

Approach used for filling in or removing blank, null, or unknown entries in a dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — outlier-handling

Approach to identifying and addressing extreme observations that deviate significantly from the general distribution to ensure they do not disproportionately skew model training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — dataset-split

A description of how information used to train the machine learning model was divided into subsets as part of the training process.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: In words, e.g. a random split of 80/10/10 into training, validation and test sets, a split stratified by composition, or k-fold cross-validation.

training-method

The approach used to determine the machine learning model's free parameters.

Required Repeatable no no training-procedure*

The methodology used to determine the machine learning model's free parameters.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the optimizer (Adam, L-BFGS, closed-form least squares), the learning-rate schedule, the stopping rule, and any active-learning loop with its selection criterion (e.g. query by committee, an uncertainty threshold). Explain the role of each hyperparameter entry.

loss-function

The quantities fitted in training and how they are weighted.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the mean squared error of formation energies, or a weighted sum of the errors in energies, forces and stresses with weights 1:100:10.

hyperparameter

A fixed variable that controls the fitting of the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the learning rate, the batch size, the number of epochs or the early-stopping patience. Numbers that fix the model's architecture are architecture-parameter entries of ml-model.

name*

The designation of the hyperparameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the hyperparameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the hyperparameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — transfer-learning

Method used to migrate knowledge from previously mastered objectives to accelerate proficiency for the current machine learning task.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. fine-tuning, domain adaptation, multi-task learning or delta learning, with the details of how it was applied.

model-performance

An assessment of the reliability of the machine learning results.

Required Repeatable no no evaluation-method*

A description of the approach used to determine the reliability of the obtained machine learning results.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. a hold-out test set or k-fold cross-validation. Validation data serve to tune the model's hyperparameters or stop its training; test data, used for neither, assess it. The scores are metric entries.

metric

A score of the machine learning model on one subset of the data.

Required Repeatable no yes subset*

The data on which the score was measured.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Training, Validation, Test. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Training" – The data the model's parameters were fitted to
  • "Validation" – Data used to tune hyperparameters or to stop training
  • "Test" – Data used in neither, which assesses the model
quantity*

The target variable the score is for.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Formation energy, Forces.

measure*

The statistic used as the score.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: MAE, RMSE, R², Accuracy. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "MAE" – Mean absolute error
  • "RMSE" – Root-mean-square error
  • "R²" – Coefficient of determination
  • "Accuracy" – Fraction of correct predictions, for a classification
value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] any — unit*

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

uncertainty-quantification

The method or process used to identify and measure the range of possible outcomes to assess the reliability of machine learning model predictions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. Bayesian methods, dropout, ensemble methods or a Gaussian process. Say whether an uncertainty for each item is part of the dataset.

applicability-domain

Where the inputs the model is applied to lie relative to its training data.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the elements, structure types or range of compositions the training data cover, and how inputs outside them were identified (a distance in feature space, an uncertainty threshold).

interpretability-method

A technique used to understand the cause-and-effect relationships within the machine learning model's inputs and outputs.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: The approach and results of the interpretability analysis, e.g. feature importance, global surrogate models, LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) or saliency maps.

inference

How the dataset was produced from the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Give it for a computation that applies a trained model, e.g. one whose task is Structure generation or Property calculation.

input-data

What the machine learning model was applied to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. a list of candidate compositions or a screening set of structures. Data from a computation of the record is named in minimal computation › input instead, e.g. with the role Source data.

conditioning

The targets imposed on a generative model's outputs.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. a space group, a composition or a range of a property.

sampling-procedure

How the outputs were drawn from the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. autoregressive sampling at a given temperature, beam search, or one prediction per input. Explain the role of each inference-parameter entry.

inference-parameter

A fixed variable that controls the application of the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the sampling temperature, the number of samples drawn or the beam width.

name*

The designation of the inference parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the inference parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the inference parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — number-generated

The number of outputs of the machine learning model kept in the dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

Clarifications: A number drawn before filtering is stated in filtering.

filtering

What was removed from or kept among the model's outputs.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. validity checks, deduplication, novelty against the training data or a stability pre-screen, with the fraction removed by each. Checks on the generated set (the fraction valid, unique or novel) are given here, as they describe the output, not the model.

docs.title: 2.7 Phase Field (PF) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0

The metadata for Phase Field (PF) data (MatCore-PF) is tabulated below. This metadata documents key aspects of the PF method to provide understanding of the dataset generated by it. This includes the fundamental mathematical and physical framework governing the PF simulation, including the governing equations and thermodynamic free energy models. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the PF computations it describes. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — physical-phenomenon*

Material process being modeled; description of the overarching processes and mechanisms being modeled/simulated.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Isothermal solidification, Directional solidification, Isothermal annealing, Sintering, Twinning, Grain growth, Spinodal decomposition, Fracture, Plasticity. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Isothermal solidification" – Growth of a solid from a melt or solution held at one uniform temperature, e.g. dendrites growing into an undercooled melt
  • "Directional solidification" – Solidification in an imposed temperature gradient, the front advancing along it, e.g. cellular or dendritic growth in a pulled sample
  • "Isothermal annealing" – Evolution of a solid microstructure held at one temperature, e.g. recovery, recrystallization or precipitate coarsening
  • "Sintering" – Bonding and densification of particles by diffusion below their melting point
  • "Twinning" – Formation or growth of twins, domains whose lattice is the mirror image of the parent's across a twin plane
  • "Grain growth" – Coarsening of a polycrystal by grain-boundary migration, driven by the reduction of grain-boundary energy
  • "Spinodal decomposition" – Phase separation of an unstable solution by the growth of composition fluctuations, without a nucleation barrier
  • "Fracture" – Initiation and propagation of cracks, a phase field marking the broken material
  • "Plasticity" – Irreversible deformation, e.g. by dislocation motion, described by phase fields or coupled to the phase field model

Note: Give one entry for each process modeled.

problem-specification*

The fundamental mathematical and physical framework governing the phase field simulation, including the governing equations and thermodynamic free energy models.

Required Repeatable yes no governing-equation*

The specific phase field equation used to evolve a field variable.

Required Repeatable yes yes

Note: Give one entry for each equation. Equations solved together form a coupled model.

type*

The mathematical classification of the phase field equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: CH, AC, GP, FID, PFC, Navier-Stokes, Multi-phase-field, Mechanical equilibrium, Poisson. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "CH" – Cahn-Hilliard: a conserved field evolves by a flux driven by the gradient of the variational derivative of the free energy
  • "AC" – Allen-Cahn: a nonconserved field relaxes at a rate proportional to the variational derivative of the free energy
  • "GP" – Grand potential: the phase fields evolve with the grand potential, the chemical potentials being the diffusion variables instead of the concentrations
  • "FID" – Finite interface dissipation: each phase has its own concentration within the interface, and the phases exchange solute at a finite rate
  • "PFC" – Phase field crystal: a conserved field periodic on the atomic scale resolves the crystal lattice and its defects
  • "Navier-Stokes" – The flow of a fluid phase; the evolved variable is the velocity
  • "Multi-phase-field" – Several phase fields, one for each phase or grain, constrained to sum to one
  • "Mechanical equilibrium" – The balance of stresses; the evolved variable is the displacement
  • "Poisson" – Electrostatics; the evolved variable is the electric potential

Note: Give one entry for each classification that applies, e.g. AC and Multi-phase-field. Give an anti-trapping current, or a sharp- or thin-interface formulation, as a user-specified value.

evolved-variable*

The name of the field-variable being evolved by this equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: phi, c.

Clarifications: The name of a field variable defined in variables › field-variable of the same settings block.

free-energy-density-term

A term of the free energy density that drives this equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Examples: f_chem, f_elastic.

Clarifications: The name of a term defined in problem-specification › free-energy-density of the same settings block.

free-energy-density*

A term of the thermodynamic free energy density used in the simulation.

Required Repeatable yes yes

Note: Give one entry for each term, e.g. a chemical, an interfacial and an elastic term.

name*

The identifier or symbol used for this specific energy functional.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: f_chem, Chemical Free Energy.

contribution

The physical contribution to the free energy that this term represents.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Chemical, Interfacial, Elastic, Plastic, Electrical, Magnetic, Fluid-solid interaction, Solid-solid interaction. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Chemical" – The bulk free energy of the phases as a function of composition and temperature
  • "Interfacial" – The energy of interfaces, from the gradient terms and the barrier between phases
  • "Elastic" – The elastic strain energy
  • "Plastic" – The energy stored by plastic deformation
  • "Electrical" – The energy of charges, polarization and electric fields
  • "Magnetic" – The energy of magnetization and magnetic fields
  • "Fluid-solid interaction" – The energy of the coupling between a fluid and a solid
  • "Solid-solid interaction" – The energy of the coupling between solid phases or grains

Note: A term that combines several contributions gives one entry for each.

description*

The type/derivation of the thermodynamic bulk free energy function.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Ideal, Regular, Flory, Calphad, Poly, Non-polynomial. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Ideal" – Ideal solution: the entropy of ideal mixing, with no interaction energy
  • "Regular" – Regular solution: ideal mixing with an interaction energy
  • "Flory" – Flory-Huggins: the free energy of mixing of polymer solutions or blends
  • "Calphad" – Gibbs energies from a CALPHAD thermodynamic database
  • "Poly" – A polynomial in the field variables, e.g. a double well or a Landau expansion
  • "Non-polynomial" – Any other closed-form function of the field variables
expression

The mathematical expression of the free energy density.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A code snippet, LaTeX formula, or SymPy expression.

unit

The physical unit of the free energy density.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

domain

The spatial configuration of the computational region and its boundaries.

Required Repeatable no no dimensionality*

The spatial dimensions of the computational domain.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: 1D, 2D, 3D. Other values are allowed.

coordinate-system

The structured framework used to uniquely determine and standardize the position of the points in space and the symmetry assumed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Cartesian, Cylindrical, Spherical. Other values are allowed.

domain-size

Specification of the computational region extents.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Give one extent for each coordinate direction, in the order of the coordinates.

Note: unit is a Length symbol from Annex U, or dimensionless when the simulation uses reduced units; the characteristic length is then given as a variables › model-parameter entry, so the extents can be converted.

Note: For a regular domain the extents are its size. For an irregular geometry, whose mesh is given in numerical-method › mesh-file, they may give a characteristic size of the structure.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [:] Length m

Minimum: 0, for each component.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — boundary-condition

A constraint applied on a boundary of the computational domain.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: Give one entry for each condition. An entry without boundary applies to every boundary, and one without field-variable to every field variable.

type*

The kind of boundary condition.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Dirichlet, Neumann, Zero-Neumann, Periodic. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Dirichlet" – The value of the field variable is prescribed on the boundary, e.g. a fixed concentration or a clamped displacement
  • "Neumann" – The normal derivative of the field variable (its flux) is prescribed on the boundary
  • "Zero-Neumann" – The normal derivative is zero: no flux crosses the boundary, or a surface is free of traction
  • "Periodic" – Opposite boundaries are identified, so the field variable repeats across them
boundary

The boundary on which the condition applies.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: The name of a boundary in the mesh file (numerical-method › mesh-file of the same settings block), or a description such as "x = 0".

field-variable

The field variable that the condition constrains.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: The name of a field variable defined in variables › field-variable of the same settings block.

initial-condition

The spatial distribution of the field variables at the start of the simulation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Uniform constant, Random noise, Geometric seed, Imported array.

Clarifications: A mathematical function, or a state produced by an algorithm or given as a spatial distribution, is described in words.

numerical-method*

A description of the computational framework used to solve the phase field equations.

Required Repeatable yes yes evolved-variable

The field variable evolved by an equation that this entry solves.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: The name of a field variable defined in variables › field-variable of the same settings block, evolved by one of the problem-specification › governing-equation entries.

Note: Give it when equations are solved by different methods or solvers, one numerical-method entry for each group, each naming the variables its equations evolve. Omit it when one entry covers every equation.

spatial-discretization*

The numerical approach used to convert continuous governing equations into a system of algebraic equations defined over a discrete mesh or set of points within the computational domain.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: FDM, FEM, FVM, LBM, Particle, Spectral. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "FDM" – Finite Difference Method: derivatives are approximated by differences of the values at grid points
  • "FEM" – Finite Element Method: the fields are expanded in basis functions on elements, and the equations are imposed in weak form
  • "FVM" – Finite Volume Method: the equations are integrated over control volumes, balancing the fluxes across their faces
  • "LBM" – Lattice Boltzmann Method: distribution functions are streamed and collided on a lattice
  • "Particle" – The fields are carried by moving particles or points, e.g. smoothed particle hydrodynamics or the material point method
  • "Spectral" – The fields are expanded in global basis functions, e.g. Fourier modes evaluated by fast Fourier transforms
spatial-discretization-parameter

A parameter of the spatial discretization.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the element degree, the quadrature rule or the finite-difference stencil. The grid spacing is given in grid-spacing.

name*

The designation of the spatial discretization parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the spatial discretization parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the spatial discretization parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — spatial-accuracy-order

The exponent of the grid spacing parameter (Δx) determining the rate at which the discretization error approaches zero as the mesh is refined.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

mesh-type

The topology or distribution of the discrete grid points.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Regular, Rectilinear, Skewed, Curvilinear, Unstructured, Adaptive mesh refinement, Meshless. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Regular" – A structured grid with uniform spacing along each axis
  • "Rectilinear" – A structured grid of axis-aligned cells whose spacing varies along an axis
  • "Skewed" – A structured grid whose axes are not orthogonal
  • "Curvilinear" – A structured grid whose lines follow curved coordinates, e.g. fitted to a boundary
  • "Unstructured" – Cells of arbitrary connectivity, e.g. triangles or tetrahedra
  • "Adaptive mesh refinement" – A grid refined and coarsened locally during the simulation, e.g. at interfaces
  • "Meshless" – Points without connectivity, as in particle methods
mesh-file

A file holding the mesh or part of it, such as its structure or the boundaries on which the boundary conditions apply.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: Give it for a mesh that mesh-type, grid-spacing and domain › domain-size do not fix, e.g. an unstructured mesh of an irregular geometry. Its named boundaries are those that domain › boundary-condition › boundary refers to.

Note: Give one entry for each file, e.g. the mesh structure and its boundaries when they are stored separately.

name*

The file name.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — description*

A brief description of the file and its contents.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — contents

The contents of the file: its text, or its bytes encoded as given in encoding. Not required in case a link to the file is provided instead.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — encoding

How contents is encoded.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Base64. Other values are allowed.

Note: Without encoding, contents is the file's text. With Base64, contents is the file's bytes encoded as Base64 (RFC 4648); use it for a binary file, or for a text file whose exact bytes matter.

link

A URI pointing to a permanent location of the file online.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12).

checksum*

A digital fingerprint of the file, computed by a named algorithm.

Required Repeatable yes yes algorithm*

The algorithm that computed the checksum.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, ADLER32. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

temporal-discretization

The algorithm, step-size approach, and integration order used to advance a simulation, governing equation in time.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Forward Euler, Backward Euler, Adams-Bashforth, Crank-Nicolson, Runge-Kutta, IMEX. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Forward Euler" – First-order explicit: the rate is evaluated at the start of the step
  • "Backward Euler" – First-order implicit: the rate is evaluated at the end of the step
  • "Adams-Bashforth" – An explicit multistep scheme: the rate is extrapolated from previous steps
  • "Crank-Nicolson" – Second-order implicit: the rate is averaged over the start and the end of the step
  • "Runge-Kutta" – A multistage scheme: the rate is evaluated at intermediate points of the step, explicitly or implicitly
  • "IMEX" – Implicit-explicit: stiff terms are treated implicitly and the rest explicitly, e.g. a semi-implicit spectral scheme

Note: Omit it for a stationary problem, which is solved without time integration.

temporal-accuracy-order

The exponent of the time step parameter (Δt) determining the rate at which the discretization error approaches zero as the time step tends to zero.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

grid-spacing

Defines the distance between adjacent discretization points in a numerical domain.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: unit is a Length symbol from Annex U, or dimensionless when the simulation uses reduced units; the characteristic length is then given as a variables › model-parameter entry, so the values can be converted.

name*

The designation of the grid spacing parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: dx, dy, dz, min, max, average.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Length m

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — description

An explanation providing further clarification on the grid spacing parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — time-step-size

The discrete duration of progression between consecutive stages of a simulation, determining the interval for numerical integration, resolution of transient phenomena, and stability of the governing equations.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: unit is a Time symbol from Annex U, or dimensionless when the simulation uses reduced units; the characteristic time is then given as a variables › model-parameter entry, so the values can be converted.

name*

The designation of the time step size parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: dt, initial, min, max.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Time s

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — description

An explanation providing further clarification on the time step size parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — solver

A numerical algorithm used to solve the discretized equations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Explicit, Direct, Conjugate gradient, BiCGSTAB, GMRES, Multigrid, Newton, Newton-Krylov, Picard. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Explicit" – No system of equations is solved; the update is computed directly
  • "Direct" – A linear system is solved by factorization, e.g. LU or Cholesky
  • "Conjugate gradient" – A Krylov method for symmetric positive-definite linear systems
  • "BiCGSTAB" – Biconjugate gradient stabilized, a Krylov method for nonsymmetric linear systems
  • "GMRES" – Generalized minimal residual, a Krylov method for nonsymmetric linear systems
  • "Multigrid" – A linear solver or preconditioner that corrects the error on a hierarchy of coarser grids
  • "Newton" – Newton's method for a nonlinear system, each iteration solving a linear system
  • "Newton-Krylov" – Newton's method whose linear systems are solved by a Krylov method, often without forming the Jacobian
  • "Picard" – Fixed-point iteration of a nonlinear system, the nonlinear terms taken from the previous iterate

Note: Give one entry for each layer of the solution, e.g. Newton, GMRES, and Multigrid as its preconditioner. The library or code that provides a solver is given as the computation's software.

variables

Explicit data structure capturing changing and unchanging elements of the physics model.

Required Repeatable no no model-parameter

A specific, adjustable, or calibrated numeric value that controls certain aspects of the simulation.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the gradient energy coefficient (kappa), the barrier height (W) or the mobility. A simulation in reduced units gives its characteristic length and time as entries.

name*

The designation of the model parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the model parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation providing further clarification on the model parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — field-variable

A physical quantity that can evolve during the simulation.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: Give one entry for each field, e.g. one concentration entry for each component of a multicomponent alloy, or one order parameter for each phase or grain. A vector or tensor field is one entry.

name*

The designation of the field variable.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: phi, c, T.

Clarifications: The name by which problem-specification › governing-equation › evolved-variable, numerical-method › evolved-variable and domain › boundary-condition › field-variable refer to the field.

type*

The kind of data associated with the field variable.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Scalar, Vector, Tensor. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Scalar" – One number at each point, e.g. a concentration or an order parameter
  • "Vector" – A vector at each point, e.g. a displacement or a velocity
  • "Tensor" – A tensor at each point, e.g. a strain or a stress
unit*

The unit in which the field variable is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

description

An explanation providing further clarification on the field variable.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: phase field order parameter, solute concentration.

docs.text:
Dataset source: https://zenodo.org/records/7319845

{
  "pf": {
    "settings": [
      {
        "computation-label": [
          "nucleation"
        ],
        "physical-phenomenon": [
          "Homogeneous nucleation (single seed)"
        ],
        "problem-specification": {
          "governing-equation": [
            {
              "type": [
                "AC"
              ],
              "evolved-variable": "phi",
              "free-energy-density-term": [
                "f_total"
              ]
            }
          ],
          "free-energy-density": [
            {
              "name": "f_total",
              "contribution": [
                "Interfacial",
                "Chemical"
              ],
              "description": "Non-dimensionalized Ginzburg-Landau",
              "expression": "0.5 * (nabla phi)^2 + g(phi) - delta_f * p(phi)",
              "unit": "dimensionless"
            }
          ]
        },
        "domain": {
          "dimensionality": "2D",
          "coordinate-system": "Cartesian",
          "domain-size": {
            "value": [
              100.0,
              100.0
            ],
            "unit": "dimensionless"
          },
          "boundary-condition": [
            {
              "type": "Periodic"
            }
          ],
          "initial-condition": [
            "phi(r) = 0.5 * [1 - tanh((r - r_0) / sqrt(2))] where r = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)"
          ]
        },
        "numerical-method": [
          {
            "spatial-discretization": "FVM",
            "spatial-accuracy-order": 2,
            "mesh-type": "Regular",
            "temporal-discretization": "Backward Euler",
            "temporal-accuracy-order": 1,
            "grid-spacing": [
              {
                "name": "dx",
                "value": 0.4,
                "unit": "dimensionless"

docs.title: 2.8 Derived Property (DP) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0

The metadata for derived properties (MatCore-DP) is tabulated below. A derived property is a property obtained from the results of other computations, e.g. a Raman spectrum computed from phonon modes and dielectric tensors obtained by DFT. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the computations it describes. Usually the derived properties of a dataset come from one computation in minimal computation whose method is DP (method-class Post-processing). It names the computations whose results it uses in input, with the role Source data, e.g. the DFT computation that gave the forces and dielectric tensors, or Interaction model for energies and forces it requests as it proceeds. Its block here gives one derived-property entry for each property, with the procedure that obtained it and its parameters in procedure and calculation-parameter, e.g. the finite-difference displacement of the atoms. A property obtained within a computation of another method, e.g. phonons computed by density functional perturbation theory in a DFT computation, is given in a block naming that computation. A result that its computation already names needs no derived entry: a transition path and its energy barrier, e.g. a point defect's migration barrier, found by the nudged elastic band (ps algorithm NEB, minimal task Transition path), are described by that PS computation. A property obtained from such results, e.g. a rate from barriers and attempt frequencies, is a derived entry.

Examples of derived properties include:

  • Electronic (band structure, density of states (DOS), projected DOS, dielectric function, charge and bonding analysis, etc.)
  • Electron-phonon interactions (superconducting properties, line widths, etc.)
  • Magnetic (magnetics, magnetization, magnons, etc.)
  • Mechanical (elastic constants, stress-strain response, tensile, yield and fracture strengths, hardness, etc.)
  • Microscopy, electron (S/TEM, 4D-STEM, SAED, etc.)
  • Microscopy, scanning probe (STM, AFM, etc.)
  • NMR (chemical shifts)
  • Optical (electronic excitation spectra, low-loss EELS, etc.)
  • Scattering (X-ray and neutron diffraction, reflectivity, pair-distribution function, etc.)
  • Spectroscopy, core-level (XAS, XES, core-loss EELS, XPS, etc.)
  • Spectroscopy, vibrational (Raman, Infrared spectroscopy, etc.)
  • Thermodynamic (free energies, heat capacity, formation energies, melting temperature, etc.)
  • Transport (electronic and thermal conductivity, diffusion, viscosity, defect mobilities, etc.)
  • Vibrational (phonon modes, dispersion, interatomic force constants, vibrational DOS, etc.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — derived-property*

Details of a quantity related to material behavior computed based on a computational materials science (CMS) calculation covered by the MatCore standard.

Required Repeatable yes yes

Note: Give one entry for each property.

type*

The kind of property computed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Electronic, Electron-phonon interactions, Magnetic, Mechanical, Microscopy, electron, Microscopy, scanning probe, NMR, Optical, Scattering, Spectroscopy, core-level, Spectroscopy, vibrational, Thermodynamic, Transport, Vibrational. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Electronic" – The electronic structure and quantities obtained from it, e.g. a band structure, a density of states, a dielectric function, or a charge and bonding analysis
  • "Electron-phonon interactions" – The coupling of electrons and lattice vibrations, e.g. superconducting properties or phonon linewidths
  • "Magnetic" – Magnetic order and its excitations, e.g. a magnetization, exchange constants or magnons
  • "Mechanical" – The response to a mechanical load, e.g. elastic constants, a stress-strain response, a tensile, yield or fracture strength, or a hardness
  • "Microscopy, electron" – A simulated electron microscopy image or diffraction pattern, e.g. S/TEM, 4D-STEM or SAED
  • "Microscopy, scanning probe" – A simulated scanning probe image, e.g. STM or AFM
  • "NMR" – Nuclear magnetic resonance parameters, e.g. chemical shifts
  • "Optical" – The response to light through electronic excitations, e.g. an absorption spectrum or low-loss EELS
  • "Scattering" – The scattering of X-rays or neutrons by the structure, e.g. a diffraction pattern, reflectivity or a pair-distribution function
  • "Spectroscopy, core-level" – Spectra from excitations of core electrons, e.g. XAS, XES, core-loss EELS or XPS
  • "Spectroscopy, vibrational" – A simulated vibrational spectrum for comparison with a measurement, e.g. a Raman or infrared spectrum
  • "Thermodynamic" – Thermodynamic quantities, e.g. free energies, heat capacities, formation energies or a melting temperature
  • "Transport" – The transport of charge, heat, mass or momentum, or the motion of defects under a driving force, e.g. an electrical or thermal conductivity, a diffusion coefficient, a viscosity, or the mobility of a dislocation or a grain boundary
  • "Vibrational" – The vibrations of the atoms themselves, e.g. phonon modes and dispersion, interatomic force constants or a vibrational density of states
name*

The specific property computed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Raman spectrum, Phonon dispersion.

description*

Explanation of the derived property.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — procedure*

How the property was obtained from the results of the computations named in minimal computation › input.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Note: Explain the role of each calculation-parameter entry. The parameters of the calculations the procedure requests from other computations, e.g. the finite-difference displacement of the atoms, are given here, not in the descriptions of those computations.

calculation-parameter

A parameter of the procedure that obtained the derived property.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, a supercell size, a finite-difference displacement, a broadening width, or the spin-spin coupling constant of an NMR calculation.

name*

The designation of the calculation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the calculation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the calculation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

docs.text:
Dataset source: https://archive.materialscloud.org/record/2024.116

{
  "derived": {
    "settings": [
      {
        "computation-label": [
          "raman"
        ],
        "derived-property": [
          {
            "type": "Spectroscopy, vibrational",
            "name": "Raman spectrum",
            "description": "Raman spectra plots of intensity versus wavenumber (frequency) representing inelastic light scattering (Raman effect) from a sample.",

Version 0.8.0

(Normative)

docs.title: I.1 Purpose
docs.text: This annex defines the identifier schemes whose values a MatCore validator checks. An identifier property has two subproperties: value, the identifier itself, and scheme, the name of the scheme it belongs to. The scheme names the rule that value follows.

docs.title: I.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. When scheme is a scheme listed in Table I.1, value SHALL be written in that scheme's form, SHALL match its pattern in full, and SHALL pass its check digit if the scheme has one.
  2. A scheme not listed in Table I.1 is permitted. Its value is not checked, and a validator reports it as user-specified.
  3. Scheme names are written exactly as in Table I.1.
  4. Check digits:
    • ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2: computed over the 16 characters of the identifier, hyphens removed; the last character is the check character, where X stands for 10.
    • ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 97-10 (ROR): the last two digits of a ROR ID are the MOD 97-10 check of the number encoded, in Crockford base 32, by the six characters after the leading 0.
  5. A scheme is added, or its rule changed, only by revision of this annex. Every field of an entry is traced to the scheme's own documentation, named in the Source column.

docs.title: Annex U — MatCore Unit Table
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0

(Normative)

Amended 2026-10-31: Rule 4 extended from generic parameters to any subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any (decision record 0001).

docs.title: U.1 Purpose
docs.text:
This annex defines the closed set of unit symbols that MAY appear as the value of a unit subproperty in a MatCore metadata instance, the kind of each symbol, and its conversion to coherent SI. It also defines the kind names used in the Kind field of the schema and their mapping to the QUDT ontology.

A validator checks that (a) the symbol is in Table U.4 and (b) its kind matches the kind declared for the property in the schema. No unit parsing is required.

docs.title: U.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. Symbols are case-sensitive ASCII strings. eV and ev are not the same symbol.
  2. Compound symbols use / for division and ^ for integer exponents, exactly as written in Table U.4. Symbols not listed (e.g. eV/A, Å, angstrom**3) are non-conformant.
  3. The reserved symbol dimensionless is used for quantities of dimension one (ratios, counts, fractional coordinates). It SHALL NOT be used for plane angles (use rad or degree) or for amount of substance (use mol).
  4. A unit subproperty of a generic parameter or of any other subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any MAY, if and only if no symbol in Table U.4 applies, contain a string of the form x-gnu:<expression>, where <expression> is a unit expression valid in GNU Units 2.23 with definitions.units version 3.19 (February 2024). Such values are accepted with a validation warning and are not guaranteed to be machine-convertible. Later versions of definitions.units are not implied; a change of the pinned version is a revision of this annex.
  5. Conversion factors marked exact follow from the SI definitions. Factors marked CODATA 2022 are the 2022 CODATA recommended values published by NIST. The factors in Table U.4 are normative for MatCore and take precedence over the values embedded in any external vocabulary (see Note 5). A revision to a later CODATA release is a revision of this annex.
  6. This annex is versioned with the standard. Instance files SHALL use symbols from the annex version matching their declared MatCore version. Symbols are only ever added; a symbol, once published, is never removed or redefined.
  7. Compatibility between a unit and a kind is decided by the SI dimension vector in Table U.3, not by QUDT's own hasQuantityKind links (see Note 4).
  8. Energy and MolarEnergy are distinct kinds and are not interchangeable. A property declared with Kind Energy SHALL NOT carry a MolarEnergy unit, and vice versa (see Note 1).

Conversion between Energy and MolarEnergy is a division or multiplication by the Avogadro constant (6.022 140 76 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, exact) and is a task for tooling, not for a unit value.

Note 2 (2π convention). InverseLength symbols do not encode whether a factor 2π is included. Properties for which this matters (e.g. k-point-spacing) carry a separate required convention subproperty.

Note 3 (mole vs. dimensionless). Following OPTIMADE, dimensionless SHALL NOT be used for amounts of substance or plane angles.

Note 4 (QUDT quantity-kind links are not a validation basis). Note 5 (stale constants in reference vocabularies). QUDT's own conversion multipliers for E_h (4.359 743 94 × 10⁻¹⁸ J) and AMU (1.660 538 782 83 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) are CODATA 2006 values, and GNU Units 2.23 uses CODATA 2018 values (hartree 4.359 744 722 2071 × 10⁻¹⁸ J, bohrradius 5.291 772 109 02 × 10⁻¹¹ m, amu 1.660 539 066 6 × 10⁻²⁷ kg). The factors in Table U.4 are therefore normative in MatCore (Rule 5) and take precedence over the values embedded in either reference vocabulary.

Note 6 (GNU spelling of bohr). GNU Units does not define bohr; the GNU name is bohrradius. The MatCore symbol remains bohr; the mapping is given in the GNU column.

Note 7 (units absent from QUDT). Ry, bohr, meV, nm^3, 1/ps, 1/bohr, bohr^3, K/angstrom, eV/angstrom^3, hartree/bohr, 1/angstrom^3, V/angstrom and mu_B have no unit IRI in QUDT Units v3.3.0. For these, the MatCore symbol is the identifier and the quantity-kind IRI in Table U.3 supplies the semantic anchor. QUDT accepts contributions through its public repository, and IRIs will be added to this table if and when they are published.

docs.title: 2.9 Geometric Construction (GC) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0

The metadata for geometric construction (MatCore-GC) is tabulated below. A geometric construction builds structures by rules the author specifies, without evaluating energies or forces and without a model learned from data: stacking or cutting a lattice, joining two crystals at an interface, inserting defects, displacing or straining atoms, enumerating or randomly generating arrangements, or converting a mesoscale configuration into atoms. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

Such a computation has the method GC and, usually, the task Structure generation in minimal computation; the computations that use its structures name it in input with the role Initial configuration. Structures generated by a model learned from data are described in ML, and a search that relaxes its candidates in PS. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the computations it describes.

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — procedure*

How the structures were built.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Note: Give the rules applied, in the order applied, and the role of each construction-parameter entry, e.g. "Cu(111) and Nb(110) slabs joined in the Kurdjumov-Sachs orientation relationship; the lateral mismatch is shared equally between the two slabs."

construction-parameter

A parameter of the construction.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, a layer thickness, a strain tolerance, a displacement amplitude, a vacuum width or the number of dislocations converted.

name*

The designation of the construction parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the construction parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the construction parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

docs.title: 2.3 Particle Interaction Model (PIM) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0

The metadata for particle interaction models (MatCore-PIM) is tabulated below. A particle interaction model gives the energy and forces of a system of particles as an explicit function of the particles' coordinates, without solving for a wavefunction or an electron density, e.g. an interatomic potential, a machine-learned interatomic potential, a bonded force field, a coarse-grained model or the electron force field. These properties describe a computation whose method is PIM, the evaluation of energies and forces used by another computation, e.g. molecular dynamics. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the PIM computations it describes. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — theory-level*

How the functional form of the model was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Physics-based, Machine-learned. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Physics-based" – A functional form built from a physical model of the interactions, with parameters fitted to data, e.g. EAM, Tersoff, a bonded force field or the electron force field
  • "Machine-learned" – A machine learning model trained to take particle positions as input, e.g. GAP or MACE
model-type*

The kind of potential used to compute the particle interactions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Lennard-Jones, EAM, MACE.

Note: Give the functional form. The specific parameterization, e.g. an OpenKIM model, NIST IPR record, or a published potential file, is identified in the computation's software (role Interaction model).

architecture-parameter

A fixed variable that defines the architecture of the interatomic model.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the number of layers, the number of nodes per layer, a cutoff radius or a maximum body order. Training settings are hyperparameter entries of training › training-method.

name*

The designation of the architecture parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the architecture parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the architecture parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — particle-style*

The nature of the discrete entities whose interactions the model describes.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Atom, Radical, United atom, Bead, Coarse grained, Mesoscale, Classical electron, Nucleus. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Atom" – Each particle represents an individual atom
  • "Radical" – Each particle represents a free radical
  • "United atom" – Each particle represents a fixed grouping of atoms
  • "Bead" – Each particle represents a user-tuneable group of atoms
  • "Coarse grained" – Each particle represents a higher scale particle obtained by scaling up the atomic representation
  • "Mesoscale" – Granular particles used to simulate microstructure at the mesoscopic scale
  • "Classical electron" – Antisymmetrized wave packet representation of valence electrons
  • "Nucleus" – A nucleus or an ion core as a point charge, with its electrons represented by other particles, e.g. in the electron force field

Give one entry for each kind of particle the model has, e.g. Nucleus and Classical electron for the electron force field.

bonding-type*

Specifies whether the bonds between particles are immutable or can be broken.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Reactive, Bonded fixed, Bonded mutable. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Reactive" – A model without a predetermined bonding topology in which bonds are formed or broken on-the-fly based on the particle environment
  • "Bonded fixed" – Bonds defined a priori and cannot be broken during a simulation
  • "Bonded mutable" – Bonds defined a priori but can be broken and/or formed during a simulation
charge-interaction

The model used to describe the interactions between charged particles.

Required Repeatable no yes charge-origin*

Nature of the particle charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Semi empirical, Quantum, Electronic population, Electronegativity, Tabulated. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Semi empirical" – Charges obtained from semi-empirical quantum calculations
  • "Quantum" – Charges obtained from quantum calculations
  • "Electronic population" – Charges obtained from electronic population analysis, e.g. Mulliken
  • "Electronegativity" – Charges obtained from electronegativity differences between atoms
  • "Tabulated" – Charges obtained from an external source
charge-style*

The nature of the charges associated with the particles, such as total or effective charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Coulomb full, Coulomb screened. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Coulomb full" – The particle charge accounting for all electrons
  • "Coulomb screened" – Effective charge due to screening or shielding by other electrons (e.g. Slater)
charge-variability*

Attribute specifying the method for dynamically varying the local electric charge associated with discrete entities.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Fixed, QEq, EEM, iEL/SCF, FlucQ, Drude. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Fixed" – Charges cannot change during a simulation
  • "QEq" – Charge equilibration method
  • "EEM" – Electronegativity Equalization Method
  • "iEL/SCF" – Extended Lagrangian/self-consistent field scheme
  • "FlucQ" – Fluctuating charge potential
  • "Drude" – Drude method
electrostatic-summation

Method used to compute the electrostatic interactions between the charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: None, Direct, Short-range, Ewald, PME, PPPM, Reaction. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "None" – No electrostatic interactions are computed from the charges. A model whose particles carry no charges omits charge-interaction
  • "Direct" – All Coulomb interactions computed directly
  • "Short-range" – Electrostatic interactions computed only within a cutoff distance, possibly shifted or damped, e.g. Wolf summation or damped shifted force (DSF)
  • "Ewald" – Ewald summation
  • "PME" – Particle mesh Ewald
  • "PPPM" – Particle particle particle mesh
  • "Reaction" – Reaction field
electric-dipole

Attribute specifying the type of interaction associated with the local electric dipoles associated with particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Stockmayer, Screened, Long range. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Stockmayer" – Stockmayer potential
  • "Screened" – Screened dipoles
  • "Long range" – Long-range dipoles
electric-dipole-variability

Attribute specifying the method for dynamically varying the local electric dipoles associated with discrete entities.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Induced, Isotropic, Anisotropic. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Induced" – Induced point dipoles
  • "Isotropic" – Isotropic polarizability
  • "Anisotropic" – Anisotropic polarizability
magnetic-interaction

The model used to describe the interactions between magnetic spins.

Required Repeatable no yes spin-style*

The nature of the magnetic spins associated with the particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Classical spin, Coupled spin lattice. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Classical spin" – Spins modeled as classical vectors evolved via the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert (LLG) equation defined by a spin Hamiltonian
  • "Coupled spin lattice" – Classical spins whose spin Hamiltonian depends on the particle positions, so that the spins and the particles evolve together

Magnetism obtained from the electrons, e.g. by spin-polarized DFT or tight binding, is a computation of its own (method DFT or TB), which the computation that uses it names as an input with the role Interaction model.

magnetic-dipole

Attribute specifying the type of interaction (spin Hamiltonian) between the magnetic dipoles associated with particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Heisenberg, Multi-spin, Zeeman.

Note: The strength of an applied field is the condition magnetic-field in minimal conditions; a Zeeman term names its coupling to the spins.

training

How the interatomic model was fitted to data.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Give it for a computation whose task is Training. A computation that uses the trained model names this one in input with the role Parameters; a model trained elsewhere is given as software.

training-data

The information used for parameterizing the interatomic model.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

Name of the training dataset used to train in the interatomic model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — contents*

Description of the information included in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. DFT calculations or experiments, and what one item of the data is (a structure, a configuration), since size counts items.

source

Location from which the training data was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A MatCore ID, web address, DOI, citation, or other description of where the data was obtained. Training data produced by a computation of the record is not given here: the training computation names it in minimal computation › input with the role Training data.

size

Number of items in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

Clarifications: The kind of item is stated in contents.

data-preprocessing

Approach used for preliminary refining of raw, unformatted, or incomplete information into a structured and clean state suitable for modeling or analysis.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — missing-data

Documentation of incomplete, null, or unrecorded entries within a feature set that hinder algorithm training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the percentage of missing data, and which fields are missing and why.

missing-data-strategy

Approach used for filling in or removing blank, null, or unknown entries in a dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — outlier-handling

Approach to identifying and addressing extreme observations that deviate significantly from the general distribution to ensure they do not disproportionately skew model training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — dataset-split

A description of how information used to train the interatomic model was divided into subsets as part of the training process.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: In words, e.g. a random split of 80/10/10 into training, validation and test sets, a split stratified by composition, or k-fold cross-validation.

training-method

The approach used to determine the interatomic model's free parameters.

Required Repeatable no no training-procedure*

The methodology used to determine the interatomic model's free parameters.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the optimizer (Adam, L-BFGS, closed-form least squares), the learning-rate schedule, the stopping rule, and any active-learning loop with its selection criterion (e.g. query by committee, an uncertainty threshold). Explain the role of each hyperparameter entry.

loss-function

The quantities fitted in training and how they are weighted.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the mean squared error of formation energies, or a weighted sum of the errors in energies, forces and stresses with weights 1:100:10.

hyperparameter

A fixed variable that controls the fitting of the interatomic model.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the learning rate, the batch size, the number of epochs or the early-stopping patience. Numbers that fix the model's architecture are architecture-parameter entries of the settings.

name*

The designation of the hyperparameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the hyperparameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

Note: Give it when the type of the value is float or int; omit it when it is string or bool.

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the hyperparameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — transfer-learning

Method used to migrate knowledge from previously mastered objectives to accelerate proficiency for the current training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. fine-tuning, domain adaptation, multi-task learning or delta learning, with the details of how it was applied.

model-performance

An assessment of the reliability of the results of the interatomic model.

Required Repeatable no no evaluation-method*

A description of the approach used to determine the reliability of the obtained results of the interatomic model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. a hold-out test set or k-fold cross-validation. Validation data serve to tune the model's hyperparameters or stop its training; test data, used for neither, assess it. The scores are metric entries.

metric

A score of the interatomic model on one subset of the data.

Required Repeatable no yes subset*

The data on which the score was measured.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Training, Validation, Test. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "Training" – The data the model's parameters were fitted to
  • "Validation" – Data used to tune hyperparameters or to stop training
  • "Test" – Data used in neither, which assesses the model
quantity*

The target variable the score is for.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Formation energy, Forces.

measure*

The statistic used as the score.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: MAE, RMSE, R², Accuracy. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications:

  • "MAE" – Mean absolute error
  • "RMSE" – Root-mean-square error
  • "R²" – Coefficient of determination
  • "Accuracy" – Fraction of correct predictions, for a classification
value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] any — unit*

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

uncertainty-quantification

The method or process used to identify and measure the range of possible outcomes to assess the reliability of interatomic model predictions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. Bayesian methods, dropout, ensemble methods or a Gaussian process. Say whether an uncertainty for each item is part of the dataset.

applicability-domain

Where the inputs the model is applied to lie relative to its training data.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: E.g. the elements, structure types or range of compositions the training data cover, and how inputs outside them were identified (a distance in feature space, an uncertainty threshold).
